body.statement:
Over \(\mathcal M\), with no upper restriction on the relative growth of \(T_N\) and \(N\), uniformly in \((p,\gamma)\in\mathcal P\times[-G,G]\),
\[
 \left(\sqrt{NT_N}(\widehat\theta_N-\theta_N),
 \sqrt{NT_N}(\widehat p-p)^{\mathsf T}\right)^{\mathsf T}
 \Rightarrow
 \mathcal N\!\left(0,
 \begin{pmatrix}V&A^{\mathsf T}\Gamma\\ \Gamma A&\Gamma\end{pmatrix}\right),
\]
and \(I_{\mathrm{emp}}\) covers \(\theta_N\) with probability \(1-\alpha+o(1)\) uniformly.  This joint-array result is for the equal-arm, stationary, compact homogeneous, marked-history critical subclass.  The cited operational-dosage model permits distinct fixed arm populations and capacity and gives separate fixed-system and fluid limits, so no upward transfer of this positive result to that broader class is asserted.
body.justification: Exact prelimit Poisson martingales produce the joint occupation and marked-score covariance without approximating paths over the growing horizon.
body.gap: The result is a joint-array theorem for the stated equal-arm subclass, not a class-wide tightening of the broader anchor.
body.consumer: Investigators obtain dependence-aware empirical intervals and the covariance kernel needed for fitted centering.
body.proof_tex:
All chains are stationary by Definition \(\mathrm{model\mbox{-}class}\).  Let
\[
 f_{\ell,N}=X_{\ell,N}-\mathbb E X_{\ell,N},
 \qquad -G_{\ell,N}u_{\ell,N}=f_{\ell,N},
\]
with stationary centering.  Dynkin's identity is exact:
\[
 \int_0^{T_N} f_{\ell,N}(X_{\ell,N}(t))\,dt
 =M_{\ell,N}(T_N)-
 \{u_{\ell,N}(X_{\ell,N}(T_N))-u_{\ell,N}(X_{\ell,N}(0))\}.      \tag{39}
\]
The Lipschitz and moment bounds of Lemma \(\mathrm{finite\mbox{-}chain\mbox{-}poisson\mbox{-}controls}\) imply \(\sup\mathbb E u_{\ell,N}^2<\infty\).  Since \(T_N\to\infty\), the endpoint in (39), divided by \(\sqrt{T_N}\), is \(o_{\mathbb P}(1)\).  Consequently
\[
 \sqrt{NT_N}(\widehat\theta_N-\theta_N)
 =T_N^{-1/2}\{M_{0,N}(T_N)-M_{1,N}(T_N)\}+o_{\mathbb P}(1).      \tag{40}
\]

Define the compensated marked counts
\[
 U_{\lambda,N}=C_\lambda-\lambda E_\lambda,
 \quad U_{\tau,N}=C_\tau-\tau E_\tau,
 \quad U_{\nu,N}=C_\nu-\nu E_\nu.                               \tag{41}
\]
The marked-history and generator assumptions make them pairwise orthogonal martingales, with predictable brackets \(\lambda E_\lambda\), \(\tau E_\tau\), and \(\nu E_\nu\).  The exposure concentration in the finite-chain lemma gives
\[
 \frac{(E_\lambda,E_\tau,E_\nu)}{NT_N}
 \longrightarrow(s_\lambda,s_\tau,s_\nu)
 =(2-a_0-a,a_0+a,a)                                             \tag{42}
\]
uniformly in probability.  Every component is bounded away from zero by the compact positive rate bounds.  Thus the positive fallbacks are asymptotically inactive and
\[
 \sqrt{NT_N}(\widehat p-p)_j
 =\frac{U_{j,N}/\sqrt{NT_N}}{E_j/(NT_N)}.                        \tag{43}
\]

Arm independence, predictable quadratic-variation algebra, and the energy convergence in Theorem \(\mathrm{diffusion\mbox{-}poisson}\) show that the bracket of the first coordinate in (40) converges to \(V_0+V_\gamma=V\).  Equations (41)--(43) give the score block
\[
 \operatorname{diag}\left(\frac\lambda{s_\lambda},
 \frac\tau{s_\tau},\frac\nu{s_\nu}\right)=\Gamma.                \tag{44}
\]
For the cross block, a control birth has limiting occupation coefficient \(d^{-1}\), a treatment birth has coefficient \(-h_\gamma'(X)\), control and treatment natural recoveries have coefficients \(-d^{-1}\) and \(+h_\gamma'(X)\), and a service recovery has coefficient \(+h_\gamma'(X)\).  These signs follow directly from the sign \(M_{0,N}-M_{1,N}\) in (40).  The edge-average limits in the finite-chain lemma give the un-divided cross-bracket rates
\[
\begin{split}
 c_\lambda&=\lambda\{(1-a_0)/d-(1-a)H\}=\lambda A_\lambda,\\
 c_\tau&=\tau\{-a_0/d+aH\}=\tau A_\tau,\\
 c_\nu&=\nu aH=\nu A_\nu.                                      \tag{45}
\end{split}
\]
Division by the exposure limits in (43) turns (45) into \(A^{\mathsf T}\Gamma\).  Hence the full limiting bracket is
\[
 \Sigma=\begin{pmatrix}V&A^{\mathsf T}\Gamma\\
                         \Gamma A&\Gamma\end{pmatrix}.           \tag{46}
\]

We derive the Gaussian step rather than assuming it.  Project the four-dimensional martingale in (40)--(43) along an arbitrary fixed vector \(t\).  By the Poisson-increment bound and the count normalization, its largest normalized jump is at most \(C/\sqrt{NT_N}\), hence tends to zero.  Its predictable bracket converges in probability to \(t^{\mathsf T}\Sigma t\) by (10), (42), and (44)--(45).  Expanding the conditional jump characteristic factor as
\[
 e^{iu}=1+iu-u^2/2+r(u),\qquad |r(u)|\leq |u|^3/6,              \tag{47}
\]
the sum of remainders is bounded by the largest normalized jump times a tight bracket and is \(o_{\mathbb P}(1)\).  Iterated conditional expectation, with stopping at a fixed bracket level and then removal of the stop, gives
\[
 \mathbb E e^{it^{\mathsf T}Z_N}
 \longrightarrow\exp\{-t^{\mathsf T}\Sigma t/2\}.               \tag{48}
\]
The characteristic functions in (48) identify the centered multivariate Gaussian limit.

Uniformity follows by contradiction: from any failing sequence in the compact rate-staffing set, select a convergent subsequence.  The moment, gradient, gap, and bracket bounds above use constants independent of that subsequence, while the Gaussian integrals defining \(V,H,A,\Gamma\) are continuous.  Applying (39)--(48) on the subsequence contradicts failure.

Finally, (43) gives uniform consistency of \(\widehat p\), and
\[
 \widehat\gamma_N-\gamma_N=O_{\mathbb P}(T_N^{-1/2}),
 \qquad |\gamma_N-\gamma|\leq N^{-1/2}.                          \tag{49}
\]
Continuity and the compact-uniform positive lower bound on \(V\) imply \(\widehat V/V\to1\) uniformly.  Studentization and continuity of \(\Phi\) prove the coverage statement.  Every identity was prelimit on \([0,T_N]\), so no path approximation over a growing interval and no upper relation between \(T_N\) and \(N\) was used.  The final scope sentence follows from Lemma \(\mathrm{boutilier\mbox{-}anchor\mbox{-}scope}\) and explicitly avoids a class-transfer claim.
